text: ITR-4 (SUGAM) is applicable to individuals, HUFs, and firms opting for presumptive taxation under sections 44AD, 44ADA, or 44AE.
Taxpayers with business or professional income computed on presumptive basis and within prescribed limits can file ITR-4.
Taxpayers having income from capital gains, foreign assets, or more than one house property are not eligible to file ITR-4.
Enter PAN, Aadhaar, address, nature of business, and filing status accurately as per official records.
Declare gross turnover or receipts and presumptive income computed under sections 44AD or 44AE.
Professionals opting for section 44ADA must declare gross receipts and presumptive income at prescribed rates.
Report salary income, if any, received in addition to presumptive business or professional income.
Report income or loss from one house property including interest on borrowed capital.
Include income such as interest, family pension, or other taxable receipts.
Claim deductions under Chapter VI-A such as sections 80C, 80D, and other applicable deductions.
Tax liability is computed based on presumptive income, applicable slab rates, cess, and rebates.
Report tax deducted or collected at source as per Form 16, 16A, or Form 26AS.
Provide details of advance tax and self-assessment tax paid during the year.
Provide details of all bank accounts held and select one account for receiving any refund.
Ensure turnover or gross receipts are within the limits prescribed for presumptive taxation to remain eligible for ITR-4.
Higher presumptive income rates may apply if receipts are not received through banking or digital modes.
Verify the return using e-verification methods or submit ITR-V within the prescribed time to complete filing.
The return is treated as invalid if verification is not completed within the allowed time after submission.
